clue.text: Attempt to reform some liar?

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it anew, so these clue letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tries to set a habitual liar on the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SOME LIAR, reshaped as 'reform' instructs, give the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: lecturing a liar on right and wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach about right and wrong is an effort to improve someone's conduct, which is what lecturing a liar attempts.

clue.text: Crazy about Irish woman, a frenzied type

indicators.note: the word for crazy goes around the woman, enclosing her

parts.note: mad means crazy
Ena is an Irish girl's name

explanation.surface: A wild Irish woman is a frantic sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The female followers of Bacchus were frenzied women given to wild rites.

clue.text: Given seat back, having had to stand

definitions.text: Given seat back, having had to stand

parts.words: Given seat back, having had to stand
parts.note: reads as someone on a bus who stood and then got a seat again, but means an MP who stood for election and regained the seat

explanation.surface: A passenger gets their seat back after being forced to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a candidate 'stands' for a 'seat' in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who stood again and kept the seat has been voted back into office.

clue.text: Type of window used in historical Attic edifice

indicators.note: the answer is put to use within these words, so it is found running through them

explanation.surface: A kind of window featured in an ancient Athenian building.
explanation.definitionFit: A window of small panes set in a criss-cross framework of leading is a classic window style.

clue.text: Very reflective and coy, hiding one name

indicators.note: the coy word conceals the others, so they go inside it

parts.note: shy means coy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful and bashful keeps a name secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' suggests thoughtful; here it means giving back light.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy, polished surface throws back light strongly, gleaming like a mirror.

clue.text: Showing emphatic leanings to the right

definitions.text: Showing emphatic leanings to the right

parts.words: Showing emphatic leanings to the right
parts.note: reads like a description of a right-wing zealot, but describes the sloping typeface used for emphasis, whose letters lean rightwards

explanation.surface: A politician reveals strongly right-wing sympathies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print slants to the right and is the usual way to emphasise a word on the page.

clue.text: Automatic response to limit service and frequency of buses etc?

indicators.note: the response is said to bound the others, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch, an automatic response
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A knee-jerk move to cut service and frequency on bus routes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a transport policy; 'buses etc?' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles moving on the roads, buses among them, are collectively the flow of vehicles.

clue.text: Compare legal right to imprison monarch

indicators.note: the right locks up the monarch, so that letter goes inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A court weighs the legal right to jail a king.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a likeness between two things is to set them side by side as similar.

clue.text: Reason given for award in action, possibly

definitions.text: Reason given for award in action, possibly

parts.words: Reason given for award in action, possibly
parts.note: the official statement read out with a gallantry medal, explaining a deed done in battle; the shuffle hint of 'in action, possibly' is a tease, as its letters do not fit

explanation.surface: Why someone was decorated, perhaps for bravery in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action, possibly' tempts an anagram, but INACTION has an extra N and one T too few; the clue is a cryptic definition of the formal commendation for bravery in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written commendation accompanying a medal states the reason for the honour.

clue.text: With an honour, pass no trump? It's biddable

parts.note: an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
to pass away is to die
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trump

explanation.surface: A bridge player holding an honour passes on a no-trump bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' and 'no trump' look like bridge, but 'pass' means die.
explanation.definitionFit: A biddable person is docile and does as they are told, willing to comply.

clue.text: Possible cause of shocking awakening?

parts.note: a rude or startling awakening, taken literally as being woken by an electric shock from a faulty bed warmer

explanation.surface: Something might explain a nasty surprise on waking.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired bed warmer that develops a fault could literally give a sleeper an electric shock.

clue.text: Facility opposing players enter in friendship

indicators.note: the players are said to go into the friendship, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: amity means friendship
in bridge East and North are opponents, E and N

explanation.surface: Rival teams come into a sports venue in a spirit of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West; East and North are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility such as a pool or library is a convenience offered to residents, a useful feature.

clue.text: Pleasure occupying a month, time quickly gone

indicators.note: the pleasure is said to fill the month, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December
fun means pleasure

explanation.surface: Enjoyment fills a month and then time flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickly' only colours the surface; the definition is 'gone', as in dead or no longer existing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in existence or operation, extinct or dead, can be described as gone.

clue.text: Animal's a long time in poor conditions on board

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull; the 's stands for 'has'
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A creature spends ages in miserable quarters on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal's' is read as 'animal has'; the 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest passenger accommodation on old ships, with cramped, poor quarters, went by this name.

clue.text: Give warning Danish cooking will take only a second

indicators.note: the reworked letters take in the second, which goes inside them
cooking means concocting, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A warning that Danish cuisine takes only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' reads as food preparation but signals rearrangement; 'will take' is the containment, and 'only' is a link word. MO, British slang for a moment, is a common crossword second.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand someone or caution them firmly is to scold or caution.

clue.text: Tree about to get repeated application of oxygen

indicators.note: the word for about is applied twice over, so it is written down two times

parts.note: CA (circa) means about
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A tree is about to receive a second dose of oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate is known by this name.

clue.text: Church roster organised to include one singer

indicators.note: the reworked letters take in the numeral, which goes among them
organised means put in order, so the letters of roster are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A church rota is drawn up to include one singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges ROSTER as ORSTER, and 'to include' puts I inside: ORISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a church choir is a vocalist in that choir.

clue.text: One tying up mischief maker? That could be wrong

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
a roper is one who ties things up with rope

explanation.surface: Someone who binds a troublemaker might be acting wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the clue pictures someone roping up an imp: the imp's roper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfitting or incorrect is not right, not proper.

clue.text: Word of address to mother, beastly mother?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is the mother of an animal, a beast's mother

explanation.surface: Someone politely addresses their mother, who is also an animal's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' means of a beast, not nasty: a dam is the female parent of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite form used when speaking to a woman, like 'ma'am', is a term of address.

clue.text: Give me a certain amount

parts.note: taken as written
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be handed a specific quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured quantity, such as a tot of spirits, is a set portion.

clue.text: Figure of speech encountered previously in talk

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: in talk means the word is heard when spoken rather than written

parts.note: afore is an old word for previously, before

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase someone came across earlier in a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that describes one thing as another, without 'like' or 'as', is this device.

clue.text: Horse for man in quarry

indicators.note: the man is placed within the quarry, inside that word

parts.note: prey means quarry, a hunted animal
Alf is a man's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: A horse is traded for a man working in a stone pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' suggests a stone pit; here it is a hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile saddle horse ridden in the Middle Ages, especially by ladies, was a riding mount.

clue.text: It'S required after one's about to get indication of debt?

definitions.text: It'S required after one's about to get indication of debt?

indicators.note: the word It is needed after the other pieces, so it comes last in the line

parts.note: C (circa) means about
being in the red indicates debt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loan is what you need when your account is about to go into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: what's needed when you're about to be in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement letting you borrow or defer payment is what someone near to overdraft needs.

clue.text: Arbiter has to come down on repeated phrase

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is an arbiter
to rain is to come down from the sky

explanation.surface: A referee has to come down hard on a phrase he keeps repeating.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus recurring in a song or poem is a line sung over and over.

clue.text: River to South-East? Wrong

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A river heads south-east, but that is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue or mistaken is incorrect.

clue.text: Elderly person taken in by senior fighting man

indicators.note: the old person is absorbed into the senior, so goes inside that abbreviation

parts.note: an oldie is an old person

explanation.surface: An old person is deceived by someone more senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled; here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who serves in an army and fights is a trooper.

clue.text: Begin a fight

explanation.definitionFit: Setting to means starting something with vigour; as a noun the phrase means a brief scrap.

clue.text: Description of healthy spread in ' old college, not totally full?

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic college, now mostly renamed universities
unsaturated means not filled to capacity

explanation.surface: A healthy margarine is described as found in a former college that isn't quite full.
explanation.walkthrough: British polytechnics were higher-education colleges, mostly turned into universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarines low in harmful fats are labelled with this term for their fat molecules, a healthier label.

clue.text: Advert about English jacket

indicators.note: the word for advert goes around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: An advertisement concerns an English jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' looks like a noun (an advertisement) but is the verb 'to advert', to mention or allude.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, thick double-breasted coat worn by sailors is called this.

clue.text: Worthily translated the Bible

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: Scripture rendered into another language in a worthy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred scripture, the text of Christian scripture, is so called as divinely inspired writing.
